source.title: Zeroth-Order Optimization at the Edge of Stability
source.authors: M. Song; Liang Zhang; Bing-Cong Li; Niao He; M. Muehlebach; Sewoong Oh

record.file_problem: Full paper text supplied, including appendices; no apparent cutoff. The OCR/flattening distorts some equations and figure labels, but the prose and experimental descriptions are readable.
record.tranche_reason: The paper reports its own zeroth-order optimization and curvature results, but it does not test any listed version about gradient-based training reaching near-zero classification error, width and local minima, depth and residual shortcuts, initialization, learning-rate recovery, or batch normalization.
record.gate_note: The paper's empirical outcomes concern zeroth-order training stability and curvature, not the classification-error behavior named in the versions. CIFAR-10 training losses and curvature traces are not reported as training classification error, so they do not qualify as rows. Its first-order GD comparison in Figure 1 tracks the Hessian's top eigenvalue, not a listed version's training-error outcome. Cited prior-work findings are not rows.
record.test_reason: Figure 1 reports the study's own full-batch first-order GD experiment: the largest Hessian eigenvalue stabilizes near 2/η at three learning rates. This directly tests V5's sharpness-threshold component using the same method and measure as the original EoS work. The zeroth-order results concern a different stability mechanism.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: the authors derive mean-square linear stability conditions depending on the full Hessian spectrum and report full-batch zeroth-order dynamics near trace-dominated stability boundaries, interpreting large step sizes as implicitly favoring low-trace regions.
record.recipe_differences: The study analyzes and empirically tracks zeroth-order optimizers using a two-point estimator and mean-square stability quantities; the claim versions concern gradient-based classification training outcomes and do not match this recipe.
record.method_sensitivity: The paper reports altered behavior for larger smoothing parameter μ (ZO-GD no longer approaches the predicted boundary) and mini-batch ZO-SGD (lower-curvature regime than full-batch ZO-GD). Its ZO-GDM stability regime shrinks as momentum β increases. These are outside the listed claim versions.

fits_no_version.finding: Full-batch ZO-GD, ZO-GDM and ZO-Adam exhibit trace-based mean-square EoS across vision and sequence models. ZO-GD also shows loss spikes and trace adjustment after step-size increases; larger smoothing and mini-batching produce lower-curvature regimes.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Zeroth-order training can approach a mean-square stability boundary governed primarily by Hessian trace, with behavior depending on smoothing, momentum and batch size.

record.peer_reviewed: Proceedings of the 43rd International Conference on Machine Learning, PMLR 306, 2026
record.problems: The empirical stability evidence is primarily described through figures and qualitative curve behavior. Training classification error is not reported. Main vision experiments use a subset of CIFAR-10 with 1,000 examples from its first four classes, squared loss, and full-batch training; the paper itself calls the mini-batch experiment preliminary. Curvature is estimated using power iteration and Hutchinson's method rather than exact spectra.
record.rows_left_out: No qualifying result rows: the reported measurements concern zeroth-order curvature/stability or training loss, not the behavior measured by any listed claim version. Figure 1's GD comparison measures top Hessian eigenvalue; Figures 2–13 and Sections 5 and D report zeroth-order stability quantities and loss. No training-classification-error outcome is stated.

untested.parts: Training classification error under SGD or Adam, including random labels and effects of model size, stopping and regularization.
Teacher-student width and the frequency of spurious local minima.
Depth-related training degradation and comparisons involving identity shortcuts or special initialization.
Effects of activation-matched, Gaussian or orthogonal initialization on training speed and trainable depth.

First-order loss recovery above the initial stability limit, divergence at larger rates or from below the threshold, and continued loss reduction during the reported first-order sharpness plateau. Figure 1 does not supply a first-order loss trajectory.
Batch normalization's effects on training speed and learning-rate tolerance, and comparisons with Fixup.

missing.what: Add first-order GD sharpness rows for the three Figure 1 learning rates: λmax(Ht) stabilizes near 400, 250 and 200, respectively, matching 2/η. The record explicitly excludes this experiment, but its measure is directly named by V5.
missing.locator: Figure 1, left panels and caption; Introduction, preliminary-experiment paragraph; Appendix C for dataset and CNN details.

record.verdict_notes: The record incorrectly excludes all first-order curvature evidence because training classification error is unavailable. Classification error is relevant to V1; V5 explicitly names Hessian sharpness. The zeroth-order catapult results do not establish V5's first-order claims.

versions.untested_parts: Whether sufficiently large convolutional networks trained with SGD or Adam from random initialization reach near-zero training classification error on CIFAR-10/CIFAR-100, including corrupted or random labels, and how size, stopping, or regularization affect it.
Whether student width relative to teacher width changes spurious-local-minimum outcomes in two-layer ReLU teacher-student problems.
Whether depth raises training error in plain batch-normalized convolutional networks or identity shortcuts prevent it; whether special initialization or Fixup enables the described training.
Whether activation-matched or orthogonal initialization changes learning speed or trainable depth in the stated plain networks.

Whether first-order training above the stability limit recovers to low training loss or hovers at a sharpness threshold, or diverges under the stated conditions. The paper studies zeroth-order catapult-like behavior, not the version's first-order claims.
Whether batch normalization speeds training or increases learning-rate tolerance in the listed settings, or whether Fixup permits equally fast and stable residual training without normalization.

relationships.condition: Sharpness component only: full-batch first-order GD on the four-layer GeLU CNN and CIFAR-10 subset, η = 2/400, 2/250 and 2/200.
relationships.reason: Based on Figure 1 and its accompanying text, rather than extracted rows: the top Hessian eigenvalue stabilizes near the respective thresholds 400, 250 and 200 over extended training; concurrent loss reduction is untested.
relationships.display_finding: The top Hessian eigenvalue stabilized near the respective thresholds 400, 250 and 200 over extended training.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
